adaptNote: Keep 'Windows' in the wife's text and have the husband think of Fenster.
text:
Wife texts husband on a cold winter morning: "Windows frozen, won't open."
Husband texts back: "Gently pour some lukewarm water over it and then gently tap edges with hammer."
Wife texts back 10 minutes later: "Computer really messed up now."
gist: A wife texts that the windows are frozen, the husband advises warm water and tapping with a hammer, and she reports the computer is now ruined since she meant the operating system.

wordplay.explanation: 'Windows frozen' means the Microsoft Windows OS hung, but the husband reads it as house windows iced over.

characters.looks: woman in robe, holding hammer, laptop dripping
man at office, typing on phone

text:
I was at a job interview today when the manager handed me his laptop and said
"I want you to try to sell this to me."
So I put it under my arm, walked out of the building, and went home.
Eventually he called me and said "Bring my laptop back here right now!"
I said "$200 and it's yours."
gist: Asked at an interview to sell the manager his laptop, the candidate walks off with it and sells it back to him by phone.

characters.looks: confident young man in suit, laptop under arm
angry manager in tie, shouting into phone

text:
The police called to tell me that my wife was in the hospital.
"How is she?" I asked
"Very critical," replied the officer
"The fuck is she complaining about now?"
gist: Police tell a husband his wife in hospital is 'very critical', and he takes it as her being judgmental, asking what she is complaining about now.

wordplay.explanation: 'critical' means a dangerous medical condition and fault-finding.

characters.looks: tired middle-aged man, phone to ear, eye-roll
police officer on phone, serious face
woman in hospital bed, frowning

text:
Last night I was out for a few drinks.
One thing lead to another and I had a few too many cocktails and then went onto the wine. Not a good idea.
Knowing I was over the limit, I decided to leave my car at the pub and took a bus home.
Sure enough, I passed a police checkpoint, where they were pulling over drivers and performing breathalyzer tests. Because I was in a Bus they just waved it past.
I arrived home safely and without incident, which was a real surprise as I've never driven a bus before and I am not even sure where I got it from.
gist: Drunk man proudly leaves his car and takes a bus home past a police checkpoint, then admits he has never driven a bus and doesn't know where he got it.

characters.looks: tipsy man, flushed cheeks, crooked tie, proud grin
traffic police officer, reflective vest, waving hand

text:
Bad Math Grade
A little boy comes home from school and tells his father, "I got an F in math today."
His father replies, "What happened?"
The boy says, "Well, my teacher asked me, 'What's 3 times 2', and I said 6.'"
The father replies, "Well, that's correct."
The boy says, "I know. Then she asked me, 'What's 2 times 3.'"
The father then replies, "What the fuck is the difference?"
The boys says, "That's what I said!"
gist: Boy failed math after asking what the difference is between 3 times 2 and 2 times 3, and his father's swearing reaction repeats exactly what the boy said.

characters.looks: little boy with backpack, report card, innocent face
dad in armchair with newspaper, exasperated
strict woman teacher with glasses

text:
Die Katze der Frau
Ein Mann will die Katze seiner Frau heimlich loswerden und beschließt, sie auszusetzen.
Er nimmt sie mit ins Auto, fährt 20 Häuser weit, setzt die Katze aus und fährt heim. Zehn Minuten später ist die Katze auch wieder da.
"Na gut", denkt sich der Mann, "war vielleicht ein wenig zu kurz die Strecke".
Setzt sich wieder mit der Katze ins Auto, fährt 5 Kilometer weit und setzt sie aus. Zwanzig Minuten später ist die Katze wieder zu Hause.
"Jetzt reicht’s!" denkt sich der Mann, nimmt die Katze mit ins Auto und fährt 20 Kilometer, dann durch den Wald, über eine Brücke, rechts, links und setzt die Katze dann schließlich mitten im Wald auf einer Lichtung aus.
Eine halbe Stunde später ruft der Mann zu Hause an. "Ist die Katze da?" fragt er seine Frau. "Ja, warum?" "Hol sie mal ans Telefon, ich habe mich verfahren."
gist: A man keeps abandoning his wife's cat farther away, but it always returns, and in the end he phones home to ask the cat to guide him back.

characters.looks: frustrated man in car, map on lap
smug fluffy house cat
woman at home holding phone and cat

text:
Ein Mann kommt in abends in eine Arztpraxis...
Ein Mann kommt abends in eine Arztpraxis und sagt zum Arzt:
Mann: "Guten Abend, Herr Doktor, ich bin eine Motte!"
Arzt: "Da sind sie hier falsch. Der Psychologe ist gegenüber auf der anderen Straßenseite."
Mann: "Aber bei Ihnen war noch Licht an!"
gist: A man claiming to be a moth is sent to the psychologist, and explains he came to the doctor because the light was on.

characters.looks: disheveled man in coat, fluttering hands
doctor in white coat, tired, pointing out window

text:
Ein Schwabe liegt im Sterben in seinem Bett und fragt seine Frau: Gabi, bist du da?
Ja, ich bin da, antwortet seine Frau. Der Schwabe fragt den Sohn: Markus, bist du auch hier?
Ja, Papa, ich bin auch hier antwortet der Sohn.
Der Schwabe fragt die Tochter
Tamara, bist du auch hier? Ja, Papa, antwortet die Tochter unter Tränen und küsst seine Wange. Wenn ihr alle hier seid, sagt der
Schwabe, warum zum Teufel brennt dann das Licht im Flur
gist: A dying stingy man checks that his wife and children are all at his bedside, only to complain that then nobody should be leaving the hallway light on.

characters.looks: frail old man in bed, nightcap, thin face, sharp eyes
middle-aged woman, cardigan, worried face
adult son, sweater, solemn expression
young woman, teary eyes, holding father's hand
